protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; five severable owner recordings under adopted D-054 / D-057
summary: The subject held frozen and the hardest parts are right. Every one of the fifteen cited artifact digests matches live bytes, every cited commit resolves, the DR-005 rider RB-DR005-V2-A1 is carried with its text quoted and attributed, and D-063 correctly scopes itself to DR-008's integration half while leaving the row PARTIALLY SATISFIED as to posture. The dispatch's own sharpest axis fails: d5721222 is not a mis-citation. Its subject line names D-035, and I nearly filed a blocker on that basis, but the commit demonstrably added D-028, D-029, D-030 and D-035 together, so citing it for three Route B selections is correct. Two SHOULD-FIX block consent, both evidentiary rather than substantive. D-057's pin list requires 'both verdict paths and sha256s' and the file contains zero verdict paths. And D-057's precondition of dual ACCEPT or ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES at 0 blockers is evidenced for D-059 and D-060 but not for D-061, D-062 or D-063 — the precondition is in fact met, which I confirmed against my own three verdicts, but the entry does not show it.

objections.location: each entry's Verdicts and Disposition lines
objections.claim: D-057's pin list requires verdict paths alongside their sha256s, and the file supplies sha256s only. Dispositions are likewise given as bare filenames.
evidence: Adopted D-057 requires later owner-recording entries to satisfy the pins in its adopted turn-3 subject, whose clause 3 reads 'disposition path and sha256; both verdict paths and sha256s'.
I counted occurrences of the string 'review-independent' in the subject: zero. Every verdict appears as a bare sha256 under a 'Claude 2' or 'Codex' label.
Dispositions appear as filenames such as 'route-b.DR-002.preview-disposition.v2.json' rather than paths under docs/coop/artifacts/.
The D-054 pin in the measured-inputs table is done in the correct form — full path, sha256 and commit — which shows the required form is understood and applied unevenly.
objections.whyOnlyShouldFix: Nothing is unidentifiable. A sha256 fixes bytes uniquely and I resolved all fifteen cited digests to their files and confirmed each against live bytes without ambiguity, so the authority chain is verifiable today.
objections.whyItStillBlocksConsent: D-057 exists solely to fix the required pins, and these are among its first exercises. A pin list is a closed checklist, and the form these five entries adopt is the one every later owner recording will copy. The same gap appears in the D-058/D-059 draft I reviewed alongside this, so it is a pattern rather than a slip.
objections.remedy: Give each verdict path beside its sha256, and each disposition path in full, in the form the D-054 pin already uses.

objections.location: the Verdicts line of D-061, D-062 and D-063
objections.claim: D-057's precondition is dual independent ACCEPT or ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES at 0 blockers. Three of the five entries state neither the verdict class nor the blocker count, so the precondition they rely on is asserted nowhere in the entry.
evidence: D-059 and D-060 state it for both reviewers: 'ACCEPT 0/0; Codex … ACCEPT 0/0.'

D-061 (DR-003) gives two bare digests and no class or count. D-063 (DR-008) likewise. D-062 (DR-005) gives two bare digests, then states only 'Codex independent verdict was ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES' with no blocker count and nothing at all about the Claude 2 verdict's class.

The entry does evidence its other precondition — the shared clauses state 'D-054, D-057, and the row's Route B selection are still ADOPTED and not overturned or superseded' — which makes the omission of the verdict precondition on three rows an inconsistency inside the same document.
objections.thePreconditionIsActuallyMet: I verified it rather than leaving it open, by reading my own three verdicts: the DR-003 preview-tm v2, DR-005 disposition v2 and DR-008 disposition v2 Claude 2 verdicts are each ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 advisories. So nothing false is asserted and no row is recorded on a failed precondition. The defect is evidentiary: a reader cannot confirm from these bytes what the entry relies on.
objections.whatICouldNotConfirm: The Codex halves. I verified those digests but did not open the files, so for all five rows the dual half of 'dual independent ACCEPT' rests on recitals — stated for D-059, D-060 and partly D-062, and unstated for D-061 and D-063.
objections.remedy: State the class and blocker count for both reviewers on all five entries, as D-059 and D-060 already do.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 5a7cc743ae58a9eb9ef5019d572871736c95586785e7a01c93797af10e0ce91b, measured three times at start and again at end, equal to the dispatched frozen digest. The prompt held at ad6d9dff…. The dispatch made start-not-equal-to-end an OBJECT condition and it does not arise.

The dispatch's axis 'cited D-028/D-029/D-030 commit is not the adoption commit' FAILS, and I record how close I came to filing it wrongly. Commit d5721222623faa854d85282df408de1c5005d19f has the subject 'D-035: record doctor-contract.v4 as DR-114 design contract', and on that alone I began drafting a blocker. Checking the commit's contents instead of its label showed it adds four register entries: D-028, D-029, D-030 and D-035. A git log -S search independently confirms d572122 is the commit that introduced each of those three '## D-0xx' headings. The citation is correct for all three rows.

All six other cited commits resolve correctly, verified at full 40-character hashes: aa75926… 'D-047/D-048: select Route B for DR-002 and DR-004 preview', 88764fa… 'D-049/D-050: record accepted Route B drafts for DR-002 and DR-004', 56973db… 'D-040/D-041: record accepted Route B drafts for DR-008 and DR-003', 7e7a636… 'D-039: record the DR-005 preview Route B disposition', 29670ed… 'D-054: user amendment', 33597e8… 'D-057: mechanics'.
All fifteen cited artifact digests match live bytes: COORD, file 08, the D-054 user amendment, and the five disposition-plus-two-verdict triples for DR-002, DR-004, DR-003, DR-005 and DR-008.
D-057's live-adoption precondition holds, checked at the register: D-054 and D-057 are both ADOPTED and neither carries OVERTURNED or SUPERSEDED.

The attack 'DR-005 v2 without RB-DR005-V2-A1' fails, and D-062 handles the hardest case in the set correctly. It pins the disposition 'plus operative rider RB-DR005-V2-A1 (D-039)' and quotes the rider's operative text — 'if the Operational metadata class is denied, doctor fails closed (D-032 BLK-6); this disposition supplies no grant or class admission' — then states 'Codex independent verdict was ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES. The operative advisory is carried as RB-DR005-V2-A1', and its Decision records 'v2 plus RB-DR005-V2-A1'. That is the classify-or-carry rule D-057 clause 3 imposes, applied.
The attack 'this file grants owner authority' fails: 'Authority is D-054. This file does not grant.'

The attack 'silent SATISFIED' fails throughout. The header refuses it, the shared clauses state 'Does not mark the row SATISFIED', and every one of the five entries ends its Readiness effect with 'Not SATISFIED.'

D-063 is correctly bounded on the one row with a split standing. It records only 'the integration half', states 'Row stays PARTIALLY SATISFIED as to posture; not SATISFIED', and scopes its condition-1 effect to 'DR-008's integration half'. That matches the row's live standing and does not over-record.

The attack 'same-commit coordinator + owner recording' fails: the header states 'Each adopted entry is its own commit (D-000 clause 4)', and every cited coordinator recording is at an earlier commit than this draft — D-049/D-050 at 88764fa, D-040/D-041 at 56973db, D-039 at 7e7a636 — so none could be bundled with its owner recording.

The attack 'unsverable bundle' fails: 'Adopting or overturning one does not adopt or overturn the others', each entry carries its own Overturn commit C-D059 through C-D063, and each has its own owner role, Route B selection, disposition, verdicts, Route A remainder, Decision and Readiness effect.

The attacks 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' and 'file 08 edited' fail: the shared clauses carry 'Does not authorize docs/v2/implementation/', 'Conditions 2–5 remain. Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization', and 'File 08 is not edited here. A later MF-6 cell note is a separate act.' File 08 measures unchanged and git reports zero modified tracked files.

The Route A remainders are specific per row rather than boilerplate, and each matches the disposition it records: DR-002 'AC-1 focused adjudication; AC-3 validator + claim-register motion; AC-4 Phase-1A packet'; DR-004 'eight-bullet Phase-1A packet; section31 v4 is not the packet'; DR-003 'full TM / V10 / G19 / publication-block' with 'Not a security-complete claim. TM stays UNSET for the freeze'; DR-005 'V10/custody and G19 demonstration'; DR-008 'evidence-side successor consuming retention, plus Phase-1A. Posture half stays closed.'

The owner roles match the rows: Evidence authority + V1 coordinator for DR-002, Evidence/retention authority for DR-004, Threat-model authority + V1 coordinator for DR-003, Evidence/storage/operability authorities for DR-005, and evidence/retention authority (contract half) for DR-008.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of this subject. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.

The Codex verdicts on all five dispositions. I verified their digests against live bytes but did not open them, so the 'dual' half of D-057's dual-ACCEPT precondition rests on recitals for every row — recited for D-059, D-060 and partly D-062, unstated for D-061 and D-063.

Whether the earlier D-058/D-059 draft, which I reviewed in the same session and which covered DR-002 and DR-004 as D-058 and D-059, is superseded by this five-entry file. The numbering overlaps at D-059 and the two files record the same two dispositions; I have graded only the frozen bytes each dispatch gave me, and the relationship between them is not stated in either.

Whether D-000 clause 4's per-decision commit rule was met historically for D-028, D-029, D-030 and D-035, which this review incidentally showed landed in a single commit. That is a fact about history rather than about these entries, and none of them claims otherwise.
The merits of the five dispositions beyond my separate ACCEPT reviews of each, whose stated limits I carry forward.

environment.gitHeadSubject: D-057: mechanics for preview-scope owner recording
environment.note: The subject is an untracked working-tree file and held at the dispatched frozen digest throughout.
environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256 of subject and prompt, three times at start and again at end; git log --format=%s and git rev-parse on every cited commit at full hash; git show --stat and a diff filter for '^\+## D-0' on d572122 plus a git log -S search per entry heading, to test the adoption-commit axis by contents rather than by commit subject; digest verification of all fifteen cited artifacts against live bytes; python3 reads of my own five Claude 2 verdicts to establish their class and counts; awk extraction of adopted D-054 and D-057 status for the live-adoption precondition; string counts for verdict paths; git status across file 08 and COORD

nonConsentNote: I do not CONSENT to any of the five, on two SHOULD-FIX that apply across them, and both are evidentiary rather than substantive — no row is recorded on a failed precondition and nothing asserted is false. D-057's pin list asks for verdict paths and this file has none; D-057's dual-ACCEPT precondition is stated for two rows and left unstated for three, though I confirmed from my own verdicts that it holds for all five. The entries are otherwise the strongest exercise of these mechanics so far: fifteen digests correct, every commit correct, the DR-005 rider quoted and carried, and DR-008 scoped to its integration half without disturbing its posture standing. I also want the near-miss on the record: the dispatch invited me to find a mis-cited adoption commit, the commit's subject line names a different decision, and I began writing that blocker before checking the commit's contents — which show it added D-028, D-029 and D-030 alongside D-035. The citation is right and the axis fails.
